_about: The vocabulary-mismatch regression corpus required by spec-doc6 section 4.4.
Each row is TWO WORDS FOR ONE PIECE OF WORK. `requirement` is what a job
description asks for; `variant` is what a candidate who did that exact work
might have written instead, having learnt the craft somewhere else. Neither
is the correct word. That is the whole point: RPN-PHIL-001 section 58 says
vocabulary is not randomly distributed, it correlates with employer, country
and class, so a matcher that prefers one of these words is measuring where
somebody worked and calling it capability.
`category` records why the row is in the corpus, so a reviewer deleting a
row can see what coverage they are giving up:
runbook_named          one of the three pairings section 58 names itself
skill_vocabulary       two names for the same technical work
title_convention_in    a title as written in India against its counterpart
title_convention_intl  a title as written outside India against its counterpart
non_standard_english   the word a non-native or services-firm writer reaches for
The test does not read the prose of these rows. It substitutes each term
into ONE identical sentence template, so the only variable between the two
gradings is the word itself. A corpus of hand-written sentence pairs would
have let sentence quality leak in and would have measured that instead.
_about_phrasings: The second half of spec-doc6 section 4.4's fairness requirement: resumes
written in non-standard English. This is PHRASING and not vocabulary, so no
ontology entry can help with it and none is expected to. What is asserted is
that the claim reader requires no particular English construction to find a
mechanism, a number or an act of ownership in a sentence.
`standard` and `variant` describe THE SAME WORK to the same depth. A pair
where one sentence genuinely says more than the other would be testing
content and reporting it as grammar.

phrasings.standard: I owned the data pipeline migration, cutting the nightly run from 9 hours to 40 minutes across 12 source systems.
phrasings.variant: I am owned the data pipeline migration work, having cut the nightly run from 9 hours to 40 minutes across 12 source systems.

phrasings.standard: I led the observability rollout and reduced mean time to detect from 45 minutes to 6 minutes.
phrasings.variant: I have led the observability roll out and reduced the mean time to detect from 45 minutes till 6 minutes.

phrasings.standard: I owned the month end close for 3 entities and shortened it from 11 days to 5 days.
phrasings.variant: Month end close for 3 entities was owned by me and same was shortened from 11 days to 5 days.

phrasings.standard: I built the test automation suite, taking regression from 6 hours to 25 minutes on 900 cases.
phrasings.variant: I have build the test automation suite, bringing the regression from 6 hours to 25 minutes on 900 cases.

phrasings.standard: I led the supply chain redesign that consolidated 40 vendors into 12 and cut freight cost by 18 percent.
phrasings.variant: I led the supply chain re-design which consolidated the 40 vendors upto 12 nos and cut freight cost by 18 percent.

phrasings.standard: I owned stakeholder management across 5 business units and negotiated a 3 month scope reduction.
phrasings.variant: Stakeholder management across the 5 business units is owned by me and I negotiated 3 months scope reduction.

phrasings.standard: I led incident management for 4 severity one outages and root caused each within 2 hours.
phrasings.variant: I am leading the incident management for 4 nos severity one outages and root caused every one within 2 hours.

phrasings.standard: I owned the process improvement programme that automated 3 approvals and saved 600 hours a year.
phrasings.variant: I owned the process improvement programme which is automating 3 approvals and saving 600 hours per annum.
